mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.2% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 1.2% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% over 3 months indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% monthly signals robust consumer demand, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise >0.5% monthly but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production contraction (INDPRO below 100) during manufacturing slowdowns reduces corporate investment and output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO falls below 100 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation, triggering Fed rate hikes that increase equity discount rates and produce negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Non-farm payroll growth above 150,000 thousand persons indicates labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 thousand for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth >2.0%) during economic expansions supports consumer and business demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 2.0% for 3 consecutive quarters but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above 1.0% and 2.0% respectively signal aggressive monetary tightening amid inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise >1.0% and >2.0% monthly but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.
